proposals.text: Replicate the underperformance test across several new domains with varied unlearning threats and check whether strategic reasoning appears in the chain-of-thought each time.
Run the same underperformance setup on one new domain outside math and treat any strategic underperformance there as evidence the behavior generalizes broadly.
Vary whether developers appear to want high or low performance across conditions and compare underperformance rates and reasoning traces to separate strategic from sycophantic motives.
Ask the model directly in follow-up prompts why it underperformed and treat answers citing capability preservation as evidence of strategy over sycophancy.
Report that underperformance without chain-of-thought appeared only on the simplified dataset and state plainly that the result leaves open whether it holds on harder tasks.
Report that the model can underperform strategically without chain-of-thought and present the simplified dataset result as establishing that capability outright.
Report the reversed-goal rates side by side with the original rates and note that different setups limit how strongly the two can be compared.
State that scheming rates under reversed goals match or exceed those under original goals and draw the conclusion about goal direction directly.
Analyse a bounded set of concrete misuse and loss-of-control scenarios for frontier internal systems, including accidents, insider misuse, and self-exfiltration attempts.
Analyse the single scenario where an advanced internal system undermines its own oversight, treating it as the dominant internal-deployment risk.
Staff the board with independent members drawn from safety, security, and policy plus outside experts, and give it veto power over internal deployment decisions.
Staff the board with senior internal leaders who understand the systems, let it consult outside experts optionally, and have it advise rather than veto.
Place the aviation and nuclear case studies in an appendix and note briefly in the chapter that they support the same conclusions as the main cases.
Fold the aviation and nuclear case studies directly into the chapter alongside the existing cases and treat all five as equal evidence.
Disclose to the public only high-level assurance that internal oversight exists, while sharing detailed capability and incident information with staff and government.
Share the same internal-deployment information with the public as with staff and government, withholding only what security strictly requires.
Treat whistleblower channels as one signal among several, pairing them with independent audits and direct checks of whether incident monitoring and resilience plans actually function.
Rely on whistleblower channels as the primary review mechanism for whether governance mechanisms function, are respected, and suffice as capabilities grow.
Start later milestone trials from a representative spread of states the model actually reached after the earlier milestone, including imperfect and partial states, and report sensitivity.
Start later milestone trials from golden reference states produced by a correct human demonstration of the earlier milestone, keeping the state distribution fixed and controlled.
Grade subtasks with exact programmatic checkers where possible and spot-check automated judgments on a subset of runs to detect silent grading failures before trusting results.
Grade all subtasks with a single automated judging pipeline covering terminal outputs, code results, and answers, accepting its verdicts without manual review.
Cover both lenient grading that credits any valid solution path and strict grading tied to reference solutions, testing whether decomposition assumptions hold under each condition.
Grade under one realistic condition where any valid completion counts, matching how the tasks would be judged in actual deployment settings.
Keep generality by estimating success through repeated end-to-end attempts scored automatically on task outcomes, validating the estimator against known solve rates on a task subset.
Replace bit scoring with direct measurement of end-to-end success over many unsampled attempts, dropping milestone structure and expert assistance entirely.
Continue using the milestone method only while reporting it as a lower bound, documenting where underestimation appears, and validating it against end-to-end runs on a task subset.
Continue using the milestone method as the primary estimator, treating systematic underestimation as acceptable conservatism for tracking capability over time.
Develop a hybrid estimator combining milestone decomposition with end-to-end validation, and evaluate it against ground truth solve rates across a range of task types.
Pursue scaled-up direct end-to-end sampling as the estimation method, accepting higher compute cost in exchange for unbiased solve rate estimates on rare tasks.
Grade end-to-end runs under both strict criteria requiring every intermediate step and lenient criteria checking only final outcomes, reporting the comparison under each condition.
Grade end-to-end runs by whether the final task outcome is correct, matching how success would be judged in realistic deployment.
Evaluate on a broad suite of multi-step tasks spanning varied difficulties and domains, including cases where milestone decomposition may fail, against end-to-end sampling.
Run the evaluation on a small set of representative multi-step tasks drawn from one familiar domain, checking only that variance falls below end-to-end sampling.
Treat incomplete rollouts as a distinct failure category and report the mean solve rate both counting them as failures and conditioned on completed rollouts.
Count each rollout that fails partway as unsolved and include it as a zero in the denominator of the mean solve-rate estimate with the completed rollouts.
Keep funding available but make it conditional on a verified weekly commitment of at least five hours, with a mid-pilot check before continued disbursement.
Switch to funding on request only, letting mentees self-select into financial support, and keep the rest of the pilot structure unchanged going forward.
Collect baseline surveys and follow-up career outcomes for mentees plus a comparison group of similar applicants not admitted, and match on observables.
Ask mentees at exit how the program changed their plans and their time to full-time careers, and use these self-reported counterfactuals as the impact estimate.
Collect structured applications on goals, background, and availability, then have staff propose matches that mentors and mentees each confirm after an introductory call.
Keep relying on personal connections from conferences and local groups, and formalize each self-arranged pairing with a brief sign-off before mentoring starts.
Prioritize a narrow agenda on quantifying trends in machine learning capabilities, pilot one flagship forecasting project, and review before adding further strands.
Pursue the full spread of agenda candidates at once: trend analysis, forecasting models, governance questions, and communication of results to decision-makers.
Restrict research to the two core strands, refer adjacent topics to partner organizations, and reconsider scope only after a year of steady published output.
Let staff pursue adjacent topics such as compute governance and near-term advances alongside the two core strands whenever partner audiences request them.
Publish the negative results with a postmortem of where the method's assumptions failed, and run targeted ablations before deciding whether to continue the line.
Treat the negative results as evidence the approach does not work, wind the method down, and reallocate effort to the portfolio's more promising directions.
Publish only after an internal review of capability externality risks and share early drafts selectively with trusted external reviewers under controlled distribution
Publish the interpretability work openly and promptly, treating external feedback and scientific progress as outweighing the speculative capability externality concerns
Prioritize interpretability directions that directly connect to the existing deception evals and validate them against the model organisms of scheming before committing further
Commit to the most ambitious mechanistic interpretability direction for detecting deception and begin building toward frontier-scale application without waiting for validation
Combine prompting and scaffolding evaluations with controlled fine-tuning studies, validating each method's sensitivity on known deception cases before relying on results
Adopt fine-tuning to elicit dangerous capabilities in controlled settings as the primary approach and run behavioral evaluations on the elicited behaviors directly
Pursue mechanistic interpretability methods that can be validated against behavioral evals, hiring for approaches with demonstrated traction on detecting deceptive internals
Pursue broad white-box interpretability of model internals and scale hiring aggressively around the most promising agenda without requiring prior validation
Continue the agenda but first run a structured review of whether combined interpretability and behavioral audits have found deception the behavior-only baseline missed
Scale up the current agenda and expand hiring now, treating the combined interpretability and behavioral audit approach as the right bet for frontier model auditing
State that expanded access likely improves audit quality while noting the evidence is limited and benefits depend on auditor capacity and careful access design
State plainly that expanded auditor access is necessary for meaningful auditing and that black-box-only audits are inadequate for building justified trust in systems
Claim robustness to latent-space attacks as partial evidence for worst-case safety, complementary to input-space testing rather than a sufficient guarantee on its own
Claim that robustness against latent-space attacks provides strong evidence of safe worst-case performance across the failure modes input-space attacks cannot reach
Require a working trained model plus correct implementations of each attention component verified by unit checks and a short writeup explaining the design choices
Count the exercise complete when the trainee trains a model to reasonable performance on the small dataset, without separately verifying each intermediate component
Check that loss falls during training and that the model beats a simple baseline on held-out data, then inspect sample predictions by hand before declaring it learned.
Treat a steadily falling training loss plus reasonable-looking sample outputs on a few held-out examples as sufficient evidence that the model learned.
Permit substituting the library version only after the participant has built the component, verified it against tests, and recorded where the hand-built version failed.
Permit substituting the library version once the participant has made a genuine attempt at the component, so the exercise keeps moving to the remaining blocks.
Specify the smallest model that still trains stably on the exercise data, with fixed initialization and simple preprocessing, so debugging stays tractable and verification stays meaningful.
Specify a mid-sized model large enough to show real learning on the exercise data, accepting harder debugging as part of the readiness signal.
Broaden the datasets toward harder and more varied scheming settings, add human-verified labels, and hold out a fully separate test set before trusting the reported accuracy figures.
Iterate on the current recipe by expanding the elicitation settings and testing the best monitor against fresh elicitation runs and the remaining public datasets.
Relabel only a subset flagged by multiple independent checks, keep the original labels alongside, and report monitor results on both versions to bound the introduced bias.
Relabel the full dataset with the assistant flagging procedure, since the known attack-prompt labeling errors outweigh the bias the relabeling introduces.
Hold both external sets out of all development, then run the relabeled one as a final check and use the pre-labeled one only to sanity-check the labeling procedure itself.
Use the pre-labeled external set as the headline held-out evaluation and fold the other in as extra test data once the labeling procedure is finalized.
Prioritize broad, robust interventions that help across many failure modes at once, and validate each candidate against several scenario sketches before committing effort to it.
Pick the few levers most likely to shift the whole chaotic trajectory, such as governance capacity or alignment techniques, and commit effort to them now.
Adopt a slow, messy many-problems-at-once transition as the default scenario while periodically stress-testing plans against faster single-mechanism failure stories before relying on them.
Adopt the converging many-problems-at-once story as the single default scenario and reason about plans and priorities directly within that picture.
Survey existing technical accounts of causality across fields, then adopt a minimal working definition and flag where the argument depends on which account is chosen.
Pick one standard interventionist account of causality, state it briefly as the working definition, and proceed to build the argument on it.
Rank the open questions by which would most change the safety picture if resolved, then scope a small set of experiments aimed at the top one before committing broadly.
Commit to the single most generative question, whether models build causal models of the world, and design probes of model internals to attack it directly.
Collect converging evidence from behavioral causal reasoning tests, probing of internal representations, and comparisons of performance across distribution shifts before drawing conclusions.
Run behavioral tests of causal reasoning on current models under controlled prompts and treat the results as the first pass at whether causal models are present.
Treat the reduction worry as live, restate the argument so its safety conclusions hold under both readings, and flag the residual dependence explicitly in the appendix.
Acknowledge the objection as unfalsifiable in principle, note that practical applications still need the distinction, and set it aside for the rest of the post.
Evaluate monitorability across architectures, training setups, and monitor designs, including stress tests where models are trained or prompted to hide reasoning from monitors.
Test whether current prompted monitors catch planted misbehavior in chains of thought on existing models and treat that as the main evidence either way.
Recommend exposing traces only where developers also preserve an unmodified internal copy for audits, and warn that visibility creates optimization pressure against honest reasoning.
Recommend exposing reasoning traces to users as a cheap monitoring gain, noting briefly that teams should watch for pressure to make reasoning merely look safe.
Look for behavioral signatures of search, such as sensitivity to search budget and objective-consistent choices, without assuming optimization must appear as a separable internal module.
Search the network's internals for a distinct circuit implementing iterative candidate evaluation against an objective, treating its presence or absence as the key evidence.
Treat the rating as suggestive but inconclusive, since strong play could come from search-like computation in attention or learned evaluation, and seek direct internal evidence.
Read the rating as strong evidence that some form of internal search must exist, since human-level play in that domain seems unreachable by pure pattern matching alone.

Test whether forward passes degrade gracefully like time-limited heuristic play by measuring behavior under perturbations, comparing against both clean optimization and heuristic baselines before claiming support
Test whether internal computations correlate with steps of an optimization procedure on a few handpicked tasks and treat a positive match as evidence for the heuristic-stack account

Compile a curated dataset of milestone systems spanning the full period, recording publication date, hardware, training time and estimated compute with documented uncertainty and source notes for each entry
Gather published compute estimates for well-known milestone models from existing sources and organize them into a single spreadsheet ordered by release date
Describe the high-compute group as a candidate distinct regime whose separation depends on classification choices, and report the sensitivity of the result to alternative groupings
State that a new large-scale era began around late twenty fifteen, presenting the separated group and its own doubling trend as a clear empirical finding
Extend the analysis to training data only after scoping availability and measurement reliability, framing it as a tentative complement to the compute results rather than a parallel trend study
Extend the work to training data and other inputs directly, building a comparable milestone dataset and fitting the same trend analysis
Fit the main regressions both including and excluding the low-compute systems, report both results, and predefine an outlier criterion rather than removing points by inspection alone
Drop the systems sitting far below their contemporaries from the main regression and note them briefly as anomalies from novel domains
Define membership with a fixed quantitative rule based on compute relative to contemporaries, chosen before looking at the resulting trend, and check that conclusions hold under nearby thresholds
Assign membership by inspection, grouping the systems that visibly sit far above contemporaneous models and are mostly produced by large corporations
Interpret the slower doubling as compatible with measurement ceilings or frontier constraints, presenting alternative explanations alongside the growth estimate rather than a single story
Treat the slower doubling as the genuine growth rate of the frontier group and report it as the characteristic pace of the new regime
Treat the record-setting subset as a secondary robustness check whose agreement or disagreement is reported but does not override the primary threshold-based analysis
Use the record-setting subset as the main confirmation of the findings and cite its matching trend as validation of the era split
Fit compute trends separately per domain and report both joint and per-domain doubling times, treating the joint estimate as secondary to the split analysis.
Report a single joint trend across all domains, noting in one line that domain-level splits were checked and broadly consistent.
Present both readings as plausible, reporting doubling times for the split periods and for the expensive-model subset without endorsing either account.
Attribute the discrepancy to the distinct group of especially expensive models with slower growth, and report the two subsets' doubling times separately.
Report the slower sub-period trend and the expensive-model group's trend side by side, withholding a single explanation for the discrepancy.
Explain the gap as the emergence of a separate expensive-model trend around late twenty fifteen while the rest kept faster growth.
Present the two readings as competing interpretations, describe the evidence for each, and decline to rank them in the main text.
State a clear preference for the separate expensive-model trend in the abstract and main text, mentioning the single-trend reading only briefly.
Compare the method's outputs against exact inference on small instances and against existing baselines on larger ones, timing wall-clock cost per example.
Report timing and an accuracy plot against exact inference on one representative task, plus runtime relative to one standard baseline.
Use the roleplay-based dataset, after confirming it generalizes better across the out-of-distribution deception tasks than the instruction-based one.
Use the dataset whose probe achieves the best out-of-distribution separation on the deception evaluation tasks.
Fit probes with each candidate procedure on the training set and select the procedure that best separates honest from deceptive outputs on held-out data.
Use the standard labeled linear classification procedure on contrastive honest-versus-deceptive examples for all main results.
Compare max-pooling, mean-pooling, and top-fraction averaging on validation responses, then fix whichever rule best separates honest from deceptive outputs.
Take the maximum token score within each response as its single score for evaluation.
Keep the auditing scenario in the suite but score it separately and confirm probe performance holds on the remaining settings before relying on it.
Keep the auditing scenario as a core evaluation setting and report probe results pooled across it and the other datasets.
Report probe metrics both including and excluding ambiguous responses, and present the exclusion case as the headline result.
Drop ambiguously labeled responses from scoring and compute AUROC and recall only on clear honest and deceptive cases.
Treat the elevated firing as a prompt-distribution artifact, recalibrate the false positive threshold on honest evaluation responses, and rerun the analysis.
Treat the elevated firing as the probe tracking evaluation-relevant features and keep the threshold calibrated on ordinary control data.
Treat the reversed direction as evidence the descriptive probe captures dataset-specific correlates and run follow-up controls before trusting its sign.
Accept the flipped sign as an empirical finding, flip the polarity to match the data, and use the probe as a valid classifier.
State that linear probes detect deception with high accuracy on the tested settings while noting the results may not extend to real deployments.
State that simple linear probes on model activations reliably catch deceptive responses at a low false positive rate.
Probe at the layer with the best swept performance, then re-sweep layers and hyperparameters on the new model before drawing conclusions there.
Probe at the single best layer from the sweep and reuse the same hyperparameters on the new model without re-tuning.
Calibrate the false positive rate on a broad corpus of ordinary model outputs and verify the threshold stays stable across several control distributions.
Use a standard general chat corpus of model responses as the control for setting the false positive threshold.
Adjust one disagreement at a time within the original framework, reporting how each change moves the estimate before combining them.
Rebuild the model with all disagreements incorporated at once and report a single revised estimate from the modified framework.
Retain the hardware disagreement only after checking its price-performance assumption against recent trends, and report the forecasts both with and without it.
Keep the hardware disagreement as part of his considered judgment and let the longer hardware tail push the combined forecast upward without additional checks.
Assign the evolution-based anchor low weight and treat it as a loose lower bound until the raised algorithmic-efficiency concerns are quantified or bounded.
Keep the evolution-based anchor at roughly equal weight with the other anchors, treating its independence from them as enough to offset the reviewer concerns.
Warn readers that the weights no longer carry the model's formal interpretation and instead encode outside considerations, so treat them as qualitative settings.
Describe the weights briefly as personal adjustments to the model and present the resulting distribution as the headline forecast without added interpretation caveats.
Present the spread-out personal impression alongside the model estimates and flag the unresolved disagreements rather than naming a single headline forecast.
Report the best-guess model adaptation as the headline estimate of his views, treating the other two forecasts only as illustrative bounds.
Start by cataloguing the cues that distinguish existing evaluation setups from deployment and testing whether models can verbalize which cues raise suspicion.
Jump straight to building maximally realistic scenarios and directly test whether the model behaves differently when it believes the scenario is an evaluation.
Probe the model's belief in a fresh context that describes the scenario indirectly, and validate the answers against behavioral differences across matched scenarios.
Ask the model directly after each scenario whether it believed the situation was an evaluation and use those answers as the belief estimate for analysis.
Run both leading and less leading elicitations, report the full range, and treat direct-question results as an upper bound on the model's distinguishing ability.
Use direct questions as the primary measure of distinguishing ability, accepting that some extra meta-reasoning gets folded into the estimate reported to readers.
Fit a sparse regularized regression with held-out validation, group collinear features together, and report which stable feature clusters drive the realness scores.
Regress average realness ratings on all tagged features at once and report the largest coefficients as the leading drivers of the model's realness judgments.
Generate realistic agentic transcripts by replaying genuine user requests through instrumented sandboxed tool environments, supplemented by a small set of consented transcripts.
Synthesize the real agentic split by having a strong model produce tool-use transcripts from plausible deployment tasks, and use them directly as deployment data.
Treat sign-flipping coefficients as provisional, stress them with label-noise and data-diversity checks across settings, and report them as open hypotheses rather than effects.
Report the counterintuitive coefficients as genuine patterns in the fitted data and describe the cross-setting sign difference plainly in the write-up for readers.
Alternate in short cycles between theoretical strategy proposals and small empirical probes on current models, letting each counterexample redirect the next round of work.
Commit the team to empirical work on current models, iterating training strategies against concrete counterexamples rather than waiting for a full theory first.
Accept a strategy only after sustained attempts fail to produce any counterexample, and treat even an exotic but internally consistent bad reporter as a defeat.
Count a strategy defeated only by a concrete counterexample that instantiates a plausible bad reporter under the game's stated rules, and accept it otherwise.
Treat the look-consistent counterexample as unresolved damage and hold the strategy only as a partial ingredient pending a patch that also covers consistent deceivers.
Keep the inconsistency penalty since it rules out the simplest bad reporters, and proceed to test it against the next counterexample in the game.
Defer the verdict until the speculative comparable-compute alternative is understood well enough to either instantiate it as a counterexample or dismiss it clearly.
Set the speculative alternative aside until someone works it out fully, and judge the strategy solely against the concrete counterexamples already on the table.
State achievable utilization as a hardware- and workload-dependent range anchored to the reported figures, explicitly flagged as an assumption rather than a firm ceiling.
State one best-achievable utilization figure drawn from the strongest reported usage and adopt it as the standard assumption throughout the method.
Describe the two methods as complementary cross-checks, present both estimates side by side, and discuss likely reasons for any residual disagreement between them.
Describe the two methods as agreeing within expected estimation error and present their match as supporting evidence that the compute figures are reliable.
Present the base formula unadjusted and add a short discussion noting that dropout reduces effective connections per pass, flagging it as a limitation to quantify later
Adjust the connection count in the formula by the dropout keep rate so each pass uses only the active connections, and state the modified formula directly
Apply to every organization on the list simultaneously since all odds are low, and keep the fallback path active until an offer materializes
Apply down the priority ordering starting with the top few organizations, and only move to lower-ranked ones if the first round yields rejections
Treat the trial project as one noisy signal, write down fit and enjoyment observations, then run a second short project or seek mentor feedback before committing to the direction
Continue the direction if the trial project felt engaging and produced output others valued, and abandon it promptly if it did not
Spend a defined period deliberately comparing candidate directions on promise and personal fit, including the nobody-cared check, and pick only after that reflection concludes
Pick the direction that currently seems most promising and a good fit, start working, and switch later if motivation fades
Derive an analytic approximation mapping the weight distribution through to softmax probabilities, then validate it against sampling on a small network before scaling
Replace sampled softmax outputs with a closed-form approximation of the predictive distribution and adopt it as the method
Approximate the Jacobian with a structured diagonal or low-rank approximation and empirically compare the resulting logit Gaussian against the full linearization on a small model
Use a cheap approximate Jacobian such as a diagonal or last-layer-only linearization to obtain the logit Gaussian directly at scale
Run the sampling baseline across several sample counts, including a large count approaching convergence, and report the comparison at each count
Fix the baseline at a standard moderate number of posterior samples commonly used for such comparisons and report that single setting
Present the method as matching the stronger baseline at far lower cost while noting it only ties rather than exceeds sampling on both metrics
Present the method as a valid replacement for sampling since it ties the strongest baseline while being much cheaper to compute
Treat each case where the condition is unmet as inconclusive and measure the actual approximation error empirically in that case rather than counting it as a failure.
Count every case where the condition is unmet as a failure of the approximation there and report the overall fulfillment rate as the quality estimate.
Set the minimum to one class and the maximum to the full class count, letting the probability threshold alone determine how many classes each list contains.
Set the minimum to one class and cap the maximum at a small fixed number chosen once and applied uniformly across the entire benchmark.
Use the exact or full-network Gaussian where feasible on small networks, and validate the cheaper structured approximations against it there before using them on large networks.
Use the exact Hessian-based Gaussian for small networks and the cheapest structured approximation on the final layers for large networks, treating each as the practical default.
Use the Dirichlet family as the approximation and also evaluate a second parametric candidate so the KL comparison can confirm the Dirichlet is the better choice.
Use the Dirichlet family with concentration parameters fit to the softmax-transformed Gaussian and measure its KL divergence against the sampled ground truth.
Prioritize work on detecting scheming first so that any reliance on prevention arguments is backed by an independent way to catch systems that scheme anyway.
Prioritize work on preventing scheming first, directing limited resources toward lowering scheming propensity and blocking scheming actions before harm occurs.
Prioritize collecting evidence that improves detection of the behavior in naturalistic settings while harms remain low, establishing a measurement basis for later work.
Prioritize evidence that improves prevention of the behavior outright, aiming early effort at methods that stop hidden goal pursuit rather than merely observing it.
Use the release-date pathway through the benchmark-composite score for the headline predictions and rerun the human-preference pathway as a robustness check on the results.
Use the release-date pathway through the benchmark-composite score to generate all predictions, since it achieved the lowest backtested error of the pipelines compared.
Run each model under the fixed simple scaffold and a higher-elicitation scaffold, then fit forecasting curves to the resulting range rather than a single score per model.
Run every model on the fixed simple scaffold with its message and token caps and report those scores consistently as the performance input for the forecasting curves.
Fit the sigmoid on all available models, then compare a frontier-only refit and report whether the inferred capability relationship changes materially for forecasting.
Fit the sigmoid on frontier models only and use that curve directly for extrapolating benchmark performance from the capability metric for frontier forecasting.
Set the asymptote modestly above the highest observed score, refit the curve across nearby plausible values, and report how sensitive forecasts are for this benchmark.
Set the asymptote to one and treat the normalized scale as bounded, matching the percentage-style benchmarks used elsewhere in the broader empirical analysis.
Treat the keyword counts as an order-of-magnitude range, report results across plausible keyword lists and years, and avoid a single estimate for the safety share.
Use the middle keyword definition and the current-year count to report one approximate safety share for the field as the overall headline estimate of the analysis.
Estimate relative scale by comparing researcher counts, safety papers, and dedicated funding against field-wide totals, then report a range rather than a point estimate.
Use the share of safety-tagged publications among all AI publications as the headline estimate of the field's relative size in the main supporting argument.
Time representative training batches for each architecture in the notebook, derive operation counts analytically, and report achieved operations per second against peak.
Profile representative training runs for each architecture and use the profiler's operation totals over elapsed time as achieved throughput for the utilization estimate.
Reject the implausible counts, verify operation totals on simple known layers, and use independently derived backward costs before reporting utilization rates.
Accept the profiler counts apart from the two outlier architectures and report utilization using the resulting backward-to-forward ratio for the remaining models.
Recalculate operation totals from layer definitions and cross-check them against another counter before accepting the overall near-two backward-to-forward ratio.
Accept the profiler counts and the near-two overall ratio, treating the observed counting errors as systematic issues that do not alter the reported estimate.
Invest one more bounded effort in installing the alternative profiler, then rerun a subset of representative measurements to validate the main utilization results.
Keep the completed profiler-based results, note the counting limitation, and move on rather than spending more time on the alternative tool in the notebook.
Instrument the training loop to count backward operations directly via gradient hooks, then validate the counts against a hand-derived estimate of backward FLOP for each architecture tested.
Assume the backward pass costs twice the forward pass, the standard approximation, and multiply the profiled forward FLOP by three to estimate total training FLOP for each run.

Estimate each model's backward-to-forward ratio from its own profiler measurements rather than one shared factor, report utilization with outlier-driven uncertainty, and note the range alongside the point estimate.
Apply the field-standard two-to-one backward-to-forward ratio to all models, sum forward and backward FLOP, and divide by measured training time to produce one utilization rate per model.

Manually audit a stratified sample of items from both sources against the defect categories, repair or drop flawed items, and report defect rates per source before drawing any comparison between them.
Use the LLM judge to score items from both sources, discard the lowest-scoring ones, and proceed with the surviving items without treating human-written evals as the gold standard.

Grade every generated item with an LLM judge on each quality dimension, have humans review an audit sample plus borderline items to calibrate the judge, and filter at a threshold that keeps recall high.
Score all generated items with an LLM judge against the quality definition and drop every item below a single cutoff, checking only a small handful of rejected items afterward.

Give defects, artifacts, and hidden messages dedicated inspection effort proportional to false-negative risk, including targeted checks for steganographic patterns, alongside the broader failure-mode analysis.
Concentrate effort on the divergent response rates and semantic differences that drive large measured gaps, and handle defects and artifacts only as they surface during routine inspection.

Keep the simple extreme-behavior instruction as the default limit test, and run prompt optimization only as a sensitivity check reported separately, since an optimized prompt may overstate the true limit.
Adopt the optimization tool's best prompt for each dataset, since the larger measured limit is a better estimate of the upper bound, and continue tuning when gains appear cheap to obtain.
Judge with a strong model uninvolved in generating the datasets, rerun scoring with a second unrelated judge to estimate self-preference sensitivity, and report both score sets side by side.
Use the strongest available LLM as the single judge and acknowledge the self-preference caveat in a sentence, since any bias affects the human-written and model-written comparisons comparably.

Include the topically prompted generation only as a separate experimental condition, and report response-rate gaps both with and without topic matching so the headline comparison stays independent of human topics.
Build topical prompts derived from the human-written evals into the final generation pipeline, since matching topics is what closes the response-rate gap and makes the datasets comparable.
Use the machine-readable structured output feature, but add a validation pass that re-checks each parsed record against the prompt and flags inconsistent entries for regeneration before use.
Use the machine-readable structured output feature and accept its output directly, treating the occasional inconsistent record as acceptable noise in large eval batches.
Build a small set of autogenerated environments scoring competence on one continuous metric each, and validate that scores order models sensibly before adding further environments.
Build a broad suite of autogenerated environments each scored by a single continuous outcome metric, targeting tasks that remain challenging for near-human-level models.
Treat the low scores on those two tasks as ambiguous, and rerun them with modified instructions that remove the values and legality conflicts before drawing conclusions about competence.
Treat the low scores as refusals driven by the conflicts rather than incompetence, and report the stronger model as more goal-directed overall with those tasks flagged.
Treat the scale as measuring profit-seeking competence conditional on accepting the objective, run a non-goal-directed control policy to locate its score, and caveat endpoint interpretations.
Treat one as fully goal-directed profit-seeking and zero as its opposite, note a non-goal-directed model scores near random choice, and read intermediate scores as a spectrum.
Run the stronger model for enough samples on each paired planning task to detect a myopic-versus-planning gap with reasonable statistical confidence, prioritizing the five pairs within budget.
Run the stronger model for a small number of samples per planning task, matching what is affordable, and rely on the paired design to reveal any myopic-versus-planning gap.
Prioritize increasing task difficulty and out-of-distribution settings over fine-tuning, since the ceiling problem concerns benchmark headroom rather than maximal current capability.
Explore the upper bound by fine-tuning the strongest model on the tasks, since pushing capability reveals whether high scores reflect a real ceiling or benchmark saturation.
Construct few-shot examples whose positional pattern conflicts with content, and check whether the model follows the demonstrated order or the actual facts on held-out switched prompts.
Compare few-shot accuracy when exemplar order matches versus mismatches the test prompt, and treat a drop under mismatch as evidence of surface-pattern copying.
Create parallel versions of the cause-and-effect selection tasks using invented entities with defined causal rules, and compare performance against the real-world versions to isolate reasoning.
Replace real-world scenarios with abstract or fictional cause-and-effect relations stated in the prompt, so selecting the correct link requires only applying the given rules.
Run the switched and matched order comparisons again on longer prompts with more sentences and harder tasks before claiming the surface-form effect holds beyond the two-sentence setup.
Treat the two-sentence result as sufficient evidence of a surface-form effect and move directly to explaining it rather than rerunning the comparison on longer prompts.
Treat the mismatched-order drop as suggestive of surface-form sensitivity and run controls that vary meaning while holding order fixed before attributing it to reliance on form over content.
Interpret the mismatched-order drop directly as the model relying on surface order rather than content, since the effect appears consistently across the zero-, one-, and five-shot conditions.
Report that under these prompt variations the model shows measurable sensitivity to surface form, while noting the effect is bounded and may not hold across other tasks, phrasings, or settings.
State plainly that the model relies on surface form over content and warn users that its outputs cannot be trusted to reflect meaning when presentation changes.
